name: Information sufficiency

subjectOf.text: Contracting parties need to postpone the specification of obligations only if the feedback process in the dynamic framework did not generate sufficient information; where sufficient information is available, contractual incompleteness can be lowered.
subjectOf.abstract: Contracting parties in the incomplete contract model only postpone the specification of obligations if the feedback process in the dynamic framework did not generate sufficient information.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560
scope_conditions: sufficient information is generated by the feedback process

subjectOf.text: Assessing the sufficiency of information by rulemakers alone can lead to suboptimal results because path dependencies may lead decision-makers to believe they control sufficient information for rulemaking when in fact they do not.
subjectOf.abstract: The sufficiency of information in this model, if assessed by rulemakers alone, could lead to suboptimal results. Path dependencies may lead decision-makers to believe they control sufficient information for rulemaking when they in fact do not.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560
scope_conditions: sufficiency of information assessed by rulemakers alone

subjectOf.text: The broad scope for contractual incompleteness and delayed decision-making stipulated by the incomplete contract model are necessary only if the feedback effect did not produce sufficient information for rulemaking.
subjectOf.abstract: The broad scope for contractual incompleteness and delayed decision- making as stipulated by the incomplete contract model are necessary only if the feedback effect did not produce sufficient information for rulemaking.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560
scope_conditions: feedback effect fails to produce sufficient information

subjectOf.text: A core tenet of incomplete contract theory, that rulemakers should act only when sufficient information becomes available, is often politically, economically, and practically undesirable or impossible.
subjectOf.abstract: a core tenet of incomplete contract theory – rulemakers should act when sufficient information becomes available – is often political- ly, economically, and practically undesirable or impossible
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Dynamic Regulation via Governmental Contracts (2014)

subjectOf.text: In the current model of stable rulemaking, path dependencies lead rulemakers to act on a boundedly rational assumption that they already control sufficient information for rulemaking.
subjectOf.abstract: In the current model of stable rulemaking, path dependencies may lead rulemakers to act based on a bound- edly rational assumption of control over sufficient information for rulemak- ing.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Dynamic Regulation via Governmental Contracts (2014)
